evidence.excerpt: Six confirmed bacteriophage contamination events in a commercial Lactococcus lactis NZ9000 cheesemaking fermentation were retrospectively compared with 18 unaffected batches using archived broth samples from 4 h and 8 h post-inoculation. LC-QTOF metabolomics identified 22 metabolite features discriminating contaminated from unaffected batches at 4 h, before any detectable acidification lag was measurable by pH probe. Nucleotide pool metabolites (adenine, hypoxanthine, inosine) were consistently elevated in contaminated batches, consistent with phage-induced cell lysis releasing nucleic acid degradation products. A classification model built on seven metabolite ratios correctly assigned 23 of 24 batches in leave-one-out cross-validation. The study suggests that metabolomics-based early-warning monitoring could provide actionable contamination alerts one to two hours earlier than conventional pH-based detection.
